title: Four-Week Sprint
summary: A high-intensity 28-day plan for learners within about half a band of their target (entry band 4–5, aiming up to 5.5). Two full mocks in the TOEFL simulator, two repair cycles driven by the error log, and a compressed final week.

daily_routine: 20 minutes: one Complete the Words paragraph or one Listen and Repeat set (alternate days)
45–60 minutes: priority-category drills from the error log
20–30 minutes: maintenance for one strong section
10 minutes: log every miss with a category and a fix

weeks.label: Week 1 · Baseline and triage
tasks: Day 1: full mock in the TOEFL simulator (full exam) at your test time of day, real section order, no pauses between sections.
Day 2: 90-minute review of the mock; record section bands and set up the error log with the 14 categories from the Band 4 to 5 Roadmap.
Days 3–4: 75 minutes a day on your largest error category, using the matching drill (Complete the Words, reply-type labelling, proofreading, or Listen and Repeat exactness).
Day 5: one timed email (7 minutes) and one academic discussion post (10 minutes), each with a two-minute proofread.
Day 6: ten Listen and Repeat sentences checked word by word, then one full four-question interview recorded and self-scored.
Day 7: weekly review: count categories, redo five old misses without answers, plan week 2.

checkpoint.measure: Baseline section bands and the overall band rounded to the nearest half; error log with 30+ entries
checkpoint.target: Profile (A–D) identified and two priority categories chosen

weeks.label: Week 2 · Repair priority one
tasks: Days 1–3: 60 minutes a day of priority-one drills; change the drill if accuracy has not moved by day 3.
Daily: one Complete the Words paragraph from the Complete the Words Drills guide, timed and logged.
Day 4: write one request to three readers (professor, office, classmate), then one timed email using the email frame.
Day 5: two interviews using the four answer frameworks; shrinking-timer routine on one question.
Day 6: section mock of the priority section in simulator practice, reviewed with the same protocol as a full mock.
Day 7: weekly review and plan; compare the section mock with the baseline band for that section.

simulator.action: Section mock of the priority section

checkpoint.measure: Priority-section mock band compared with its baseline band; count of entries in the priority category
checkpoint.target: Priority section at or above its baseline band and fewer priority-category misses than week 1

weeks.label: Week 3 · Full mock 2 and repair two
tasks: Day 1: full mock 2 in the TOEFL simulator under the same conditions as mock 1.
Day 2: 90-minute review; compare both mocks section by section and recount the error categories.
Days 3–5: 60–75 minutes a day on the largest category from mock 2, plus 20 minutes of maintenance.
Day 5: decide whether to keep the test date; ETS requires rescheduling at least four full days before the test.
Day 6: one timed email, one discussion post, seven Listen and Repeat sentences and one interview.
Day 7: confirm free score recipients (the Bulletin deadline is 10 p.m. local test-center time the day before the test) and write your top-ten error list.

checkpoint.measure: Mock 2 section bands and overall band versus mock 1
checkpoint.target: Overall at target or within half a band of it, with no section more than one band below the target

weeks.label: Week 4 · Final days and test
tasks: Days 1–2: 60 minutes a day: one short set of each section plus repair of your top-ten list.
Day 3: Home Edition: equipment check on the same weekday and time as the test, room set-up rehearsal; test center: route and arrival time (30 minutes early).
Day 4: 30 minutes of light mixed practice; ID checked against your ETS account name.
Day before the test: 20-minute warm-up only, read the top-ten list, pack, sleep at the usual time.
Test day: follow the test-center or Home Edition routine from the Final 14 Days guide; decide report or cancel by the rule you wrote in advance.

checkpoint.measure: Logistics checklist complete; top-ten error list written
checkpoint.target: Test taken with the planned routine; report-or-cancel decision made by rule, not by mood

checkpoints.target_band: Priority section at or above baseline

decision_rules: If mock 2 is more than half a band below target overall, consider rescheduling and switching to the Eight-Week Standard plan.
If a priority category has not shrunk after one week, change the drill rather than adding hours.
Never schedule a full mock in the last three days before the test.

metadata.recommended_for: A test date about four weeks away and a gap of half a band or less.
metadata.score_window_basis: score_min/score_max are the ETS 0-120 comparison totals for band 4 (72+) and the top of band 5.5 (113); band windows are in band_*
metadata.guarantee: none: practice plan, not a score prediction
